t: The edicts are the earliest written and datable texts from India, and because they were cut in stone they survive as they were first inscribed, unlike the Vedic texts, which were composed and handed down orally.

They set out a policy of dhamma, an ethic of non-violence, tolerance of all sects, obedience to parents and humane treatment of servants, which Romila Thapar describes as one to which no religious or social group could object.
The Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts of the edicts had become extinct by about the 5th century CE, and were deciphered in the 1830s by Christian Lassen and James Prinsep.
dyk: In Minor Rock Edict No. 1 Ashoka says he had been on tour for 256 days, and the numeral 6 in that number is counted among the earliest ancestors of the digit used today.
ev: The Kandahar Bilingual Rock Inscription, in Greek and Aramaic, is written in the 10th year of Ashoka's reign at the border of his empire with the Hellenistic world
The Minor Pillar Edicts begin, from the 12th year of Ashoka's reign
Major Rock Edict No. 13, which names Hellenistic kings, is dated to about the 14th year of the reign
The Major Pillar Edicts are inscribed from the 26th and 27th years of the reign, the most technically elegant of the inscriptions
The Chinese traveller Fa Hian refers to one of Ashoka's pillar edicts at Ni-li, an edict that has not been found
Christian Lassen makes the first successful attempt to decipher Brahmi, using the bilingual Greek-Brahmi coins of Agathocles
James Prinsep publishes translations of a large number of rock edicts, after identifying the rest of the Brahmi characters
An inscription found at Maski confirms that the title Devanampiya belongs to Ashoka

f.made: Attributed to Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire, who ruled from 268 to 232 BCE; engraved on his order, mostly in Prakrit, with some Greek and Aramaic versions in the northwest
f.form: More than thirty inscriptions in four groups: Minor Rock Edicts, Minor Pillar Edicts, 14 Major Rock Edicts (with 2 separate ones in Odisha) and 7 Major Pillar Edicts; written in Ashokan Prakrit, Greek and Aramaic, in the Brahmi and Kharoshthi scripts and the Greek and Aramaic scripts
f.where: On rocks, cave walls and pillars across modern India, Bangladesh, Nepal, Afghanistan and Pakistan; the Kandahar inscriptions stand in the city of Old Kandahar in Afghanistan
f.known: the earliest written and datable texts from India; the policy of dhamma; the remorse after the Kalinga conquest; the Greek kings named in Major Rock Edict No. 13; the Rummindei Edict naming Lumbini as the Buddha's birthplace; early Brahmi numerals; their decipherment by James Prinsep in 1838
